comments: REPLACE_WITH_REVIEW_COMMENTS. Approving this gate promotes features/generated/home-navigation/home-icon-navigation.feature into features/approved/, which is the only input to bddgen, and authorises the first TypeScript to be written for this capability. Three things need your explicit acceptance rather than your silence. First, no locator has been verified. Every one will be written as MCP_VALIDATION_REQUIRED and replaced only by the Playwright Test Planner against the real application; two of them - the Command Center control, which exposes no accessible name at all, and the dashboard icons, which must be scoped to avoid colliding with the header links of the same name - will need written VALIDATED waivers rather than accessible locators. Second, TS-ETA-411-008 and TS-ETA-411-009 are written against link addresses that were never walked; approving them authorises the code, not the expectation, and PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION must confirm both destinations before they can be trusted. Third, AMB-ETA-411-006 is still unanswered and no amount of application observation will close it, because whether the menu link labelled Organization counts as a header route to Preferences is a question of intent rather than markup. Please also confirm that the wording distinguishing the dashboard icons from the header links is clear enough to survive a later tidy-up of the step definitions; if it is not obvious to you on a first read, it will not be obvious to whoever refactors it, and two acceptance criteria would begin reporting coverage that only one of them has.

itemDecisions.comment: Scenario: A successful organization sign-in places the user on the Home page. The only scenario that exercises signing in as behaviour; the other eight consume the session as a precondition. Reuses three existing steps from the account-access capability verbatim.
Scenario: The Home page presents three activatable icons. Asserts presence and activatability only, and names the icons as the Home page dashboard icons rather than the header links of the same name.

Scenario: The New Transaction icon reaches the New Transaction page. The only destination offering an element unique to it, so this scenario asserts more than arrival. Uses the dashboard icon, not the header link - the distinction from TS-ETA-411-008 is load-bearing.

Scenario: The Workspace icon reaches the Workspace page. Arrival only. The destination exposes nothing unique and every page returns the same browser title, so this will pass on a page that arrived and then failed to render. Knowingly accepted as AMB-ETA-411-002.
Scenario: The Preferences icon reaches the Preferences page. Arrival only, as above, and the single approved route to this page while AMB-ETA-411-006 is open.

Scenario Outline: The Command Center control returns the user Home from each destination. The criterion says any Home page icon, so all three return legs are walked through an Examples table rather than one being walked and two inferred. One scenario id, three executions. Asserts the outcome only, never how the control is labelled - it has no accessible name.

Scenario: The header navigation offers New Transaction and Workspace links. Exactly two duplicates, not three. Also asserts the links are distinct from the dashboard icons of the same name, which is the guard against TS-ETA-411-003 and TS-ETA-411-008 collapsing into one test.

Scenario: The header New Transaction link reaches the New Transaction page. UNCONFIRMED DESTINATION - the expected page comes from the link address and was never navigated. Approving authorises the code; PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION must confirm the destination. See RISK-TP-ETA-411-001.

Scenario: The header Workspace link reaches the Workspace page. UNCONFIRMED DESTINATION, as above. Must exercise the header link rather than the dashboard icon, or it silently duplicates TS-ETA-411-004.
